recommendations: Consider tightening SR1 to explicitly reject reports that list bit 7 alongside spurious additional bits without justification, since current logic accepts any list containing 7 regardless of extra noise bits.

Consider adding an explicit check in SR3/SR4 that rejects reports referencing RTL constructs from unrelated or hallucinated signal names not present in scratchpad_lookup.v, to further harden against superficial keyword-stuffing submissions.

requirement_results.evidence: RTL, design_brief.md, fault_model.json, and testbench_timing.v are mutually consistent with the hidden ground truth (index[7] selects fast/slow bank, 1 vs 3 cycles, formulas i*3+1 and i*5+2). The golden report and grader align with this ground truth.

Differential run shows golden_run exit_code 0 with all 8 [TEST] PASS lines, and vulnerable_run (naive baseline) exit_code 1 with FR1, FR3, FR4, SR1, SR2, SR3, SR4 failing (only FR2 passes since a boolean is present).
requirement_results.requirement: evaluate.py accepts correct submission and rejects baseline

requirement_results.evidence: FR1-FR4 map to format_conformance; SR1/SR2 map to leakage_detection_accuracy and fault_coverage; SR3 covers fault_coverage (divergent paths); SR4 covers hardening_precision. All four eval.metrics are represented by requirement checks.
requirement_map explicitly labels FR1-FR4 as 'functional' and SR1-SR4 as 'security', each with distinct detection logic and test files.
requirement_results.requirement: Requirement map separates functional and security requirements

requirement_results.evidence: evaluation/tb_leak_check.v actively compiles and simulates the DUT with iverilog/vvp to obtain ground-truth cycle counts for index[7]=0 and index[7]=1, rather than relying solely on static text matching; SR2 cross-validates submitted latency against this simulation.

All referenced files (scratchpad_lookup.v, fault_model.json, design_brief.md, testbench_timing.v, tb_leak_check.v, evaluate.py) are provided in the bundles; no external dependencies beyond iverilog/vvp which are declared toolchain requirements. No unsafe operations present.

The artifacts implement a concrete side-channel timing leak (CWE-208/385/203-relevant) with FSM states S_FAST_WAIT/S_SLOW_WAIT1-3, a specific leaking bit (index[7]), and cycle-accurate timing contract, directly tailored to side_channel_fault_analysis domain rather than generic vulnerability text.
requirement_results.requirement: Benchmark adapted to domain rather than generic filler

requirement_results.evidence: SR2 ground truth is derived by independently simulating the DUT via iverilog/vvp with a dedicated harness (tb_leak_check.v) rather than hardcoded values alone, and coverage/mutation scores in the validation report are 1.0 with no dead checks or uncovered requirements.

README.md, metadata.json, design_brief.md, and fault_model.json use neutral engineering language ('characterize timing variation', 'observation model') without naming CWE ids, SR ids, or explicitly stating the module is vulnerable; scratchpad_lookup.v contains no security-flagging comments.
requirement_results.requirement: No leakage of hidden intent in public-facing artifacts

requirement_results.evidence: FR1-FR4 specify exact field names, types, and values (module_under_test=='scratchpad_lookup', functional_correctness_confirmed boolean, latency_measurements array of 2 typed objects, report_format_version=='1.0'), each independently verifiable via the pinned JSON schema and grader logic.
